technical.prompt: What is the difference between top-down and bottom-up budgeting?

choices.answer: Top-down starts from leadership targets; bottom-up from units

technical.prompt: What is a flexed budget?

choices.answer: A budget restated for the volume actually achieved
distractors: A budget that changes every day
A budget with no fixed costs

technical.prompt: What is the difference between a cost centre and a profit centre?

choices.answer: Cost centres own costs; profit centres own profit
distractors: Both are measured the same way
Cost centres earn all the revenue

technical.prompt: What makes a variance favourable or unfavourable?

choices.answer: Whether it raises or lowers profit compared with plan
distractors: Whether it is large or small

technical.prompt: What is an FX variance?
expectedPoints: Effect of exchange rates vs budget rate

choices.answer: The effect of exchange rates differing from budget rates
distractors: A difference in staff between countries

technical.prompt: What does constant currency reporting show?

choices.answer: Results at fixed rates, showing underlying trends
distractors: Results in the local currency only
Results at the year-end exchange rate

technical.prompt: What is forecast accuracy, and why track it?

choices.answer: How close forecasts come to actuals, which reveals bias

technical.prompt: What is forecast bias?

choices.answer: A consistent tendency to forecast too high or too low
distractors: A forecast made by one person

technical.prompt: How does seasonality affect forecasting?

choices.answer: Uneven sales patterns mean early months can mislead

technical.prompt: What is headcount planning?

choices.answer: Forecasting staff numbers and costs
distractors: Counting staff in the office daily

technical.prompt: What is a fully loaded employee cost?

choices.answer: Salary plus benefits, payroll taxes and other on-costs
distractors: The cost of an employee's equipment

technical.prompt: What is a vacancy factor in a headcount budget?

choices.answer: An allowance for roles left unfilled
distractors: A penalty charged for staff turnover

technical.prompt: What is an EBITDA bridge?
expectedPoints: Walks from one EBITDA to another

choices.answer: A walk from one EBITDA to another by driver
distractors: A loan taken out to fund EBITDA
A chart of the share price
A list of every single cost line

technical.prompt: What is an accrual in management accounts?
expectedPoints: Recording costs or revenue when incurred

choices.answer: Recording costs or revenue in the period they arise

technical.prompt: What is scenario planning in FP&A?

choices.answer: Base, upside and downside cases

technical.prompt: What is a run-rate?

choices.answer: Recent performance annualised to show the current pace
distractors: The speed of a company's systems
The rate at which staff leave

technical.prompt: Why are capital expenditure budgets managed separately from operating budgets?

choices.answer: Long-lived investments need their own approvals
distractors: Capex has no effect on cash
Capex is always too small to matter

technical.prompt: Why is budget ownership by business leaders important?

choices.answer: Leaders who own budgets are accountable for delivering them

technical.prompt: What makes a management dashboard useful?

choices.answer: A few key metrics with trends and targets
distractors: Every metric the systems can produce

technical.prompt: Budget: 10,000 units, $20 variable cost each, $100,000 fixed. Actual volume was 12,000 and costs $360,000. What is the spending variance against the flexed budget?

choices.answer: $20,000 unfavourable

technical.prompt: Product A earns $40 of contribution a unit and B $20. Budget was 10,000 units at a 50/50 mix; actual volume was also 10,000 units but at a 30/70 mix. What is the mix variance?

choices.answer: $40,000 unfavourable

technical.prompt: Budget revenue was EUR 10 million at $1.10. The actual rate was $1.05, with euro sales on budget. What is the FX variance in dollars?

choices.answer: $500,000 unfavourable

technical.prompt: A company plans 20 hires at $80,000 salary with 25% on-costs, all starting mid-year. What is the in-year cost?

choices.answer: About $1 million

technical.prompt: 200 budgeted roles cost $90,000 each fully loaded, with a 5% vacancy factor. What is the budget?

choices.answer: About $17.1 million

technical.prompt: Three months were forecast at 100, 110 and 90; actuals were 110, 100 and 90. What is the mean absolute percentage error?
expectedPoints: Direction differs, so no clear bias

choices.answer: About 6.4%

technical.prompt: EBITDA was $50 million. Volume added $8 million and price added $3 million, while cost inflation reduced it by $6 million and FX by $2 million. What is EBITDA now?
expectedPoints: Cost inflation offset part of the gains

choices.answer: $53 million

technical.prompt: Base case profit is $100 million (60% likely), downside $80 million (25%) and upside $120 million (15%). What is the expected profit?

choices.answer: $98 million

technical.prompt: Fourth-quarter operating costs were $30 million, while the full year was $110 million. What is the run-rate, and what does it suggest?

choices.answer: $120 million, suggesting costs are rising

technical.prompt: Q4 usually delivers 40% of annual sales. Sales for the first three quarters total $60 million. What is a sensible full-year forecast?

choices.answer: About $100 million

technical.prompt: Last year's costs were $80 million. Next year assumes 5% cost inflation and 10% volume growth, and all costs scale with volume. What is the cost budget?

choices.answer: $92.4 million

technical.prompt: Why should a variance report separate controllable from uncontrollable factors?

choices.answer: Managers should answer only for what they control
distractors: It helps to hide weak performance

technical.prompt: Why might a flexed budget show a manager performing well even though costs exceeded the original budget?

choices.answer: Higher volume justified higher costs
distractors: Costs above budget are always good

technical.prompt: How would you detect sandbagging in business unit forecasts?

choices.answer: Units that beat forecasts every period
distractors: Units that miss forecasts every time

technical.prompt: Why does hiring timing matter so much in a headcount budget?
expectedPoints: In-year cost depends on start date

choices.answer: Start dates shift in-year and full-year costs

technical.prompt: What is the danger of using run-rates for seasonal businesses?

choices.answer: A peak or trough quarter gets wrongly annualised
distractors: They only fail for flat businesses

technical.prompt: How should a business partner challenge a sales team's revenue forecast?

choices.answer: Test pipeline quality, conversion rates and track record
distractors: Accept it, since sales knows best
Replace it with last year's number
